heroHeadline: IFT-12 RESULT: Ship 39 Indian Ocean Splashdown — Booster 19 Lost After Boostback Anomaly; FAA Investigation Launched; Artemis III to Fly With Structural Spacer
heroSubtitle: May 22-24: SpaceX's Starship IFT-12 launched at 22:30 UTC May 22 from Orbital Launch Pad 2 (OLP-2), Starbase — the maiden flight of Starship V3 (Block 3, Booster 19 + Ship 39). Ship 39 reached a valid suborbital trajectory, deployed 22 Starlink V3 simulators, withstood reentry (Elon Musk: 'V3 heat shield held well'), and splashed down nominally in the Indian Ocean. Booster 19 (33 Raptor 3 engines, all ignited at liftoff) suffered a boostback burn anomaly: multiple engines failed to fire, causing uncontrolled spin and Gulf of Mexico crash at high velocity. The FAA confirmed it is aware of the anomaly and launched a mishap assessment expected to conclude by June 2026; SpaceX must receive FAA sign-off before IFT-13 can proceed. The NASA-required docking port and propellant-transfer interface hardware aboard Ship 39 survived the flight — a structural precursor milestone for Artemis III HLS qualification — though no active transfer test was conducted. On May 24, NASA confirmed Artemis III will fly with an inert structural spacer instead of the Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS) upper stage; the sole remaining ICPS is reserved for Artemis IV (first crewed lunar landing, ~2028). Marshall Space Flight Center has begun fabricating the spacer's barrel section and rings. Artemis II crew — Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialist Christina Koch, and Canadian Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen — are on Day 44 post-splashdown at Johnson Space Center continuing reconditioning.
